issue.title: [Media clock] Phase-align the recovered media clock to the followed stream (IEEE 1722-2016 10.8, 4.3.5)
issue.body:
[A10] Filed from the #629 design (PR #631, lane M1, decision D7). This is a pre-existing gap of the CRF-following path, outside #629's acceptance; AAF following would inherit it.

## The gap

The media servo locks frequency only (`hdl/ieee1722/crf/KL_mmcm_drp_servo.sv:27-30` at dev `d4dd7426`). Nothing aligns the DUT's talker presentation times with the followed stream's timing points. So these hold only by chance:
- IEEE 1722-2016 10.8: a talker following CRF stays within ±5 % of a sample period;
- IEEE 1722-2016 4.3.5: streams generated from a recovered stream fall on whole periods.

## Work

- [ ] Add a phase term to the media-clock chain (for example the CRF delta, or the followed AAF timestamp against the local grid) that feeds the grid aligner's lock target, not a second master.
- [ ] Define the phase contract per source (CRF, AAF) in `docs/design/MEDIA_CLOCK_FOLLOWING.md`.

## Proof and acceptance

- [ ] **Simulation:** a phase step on the followed stream is pulled into ±5 % of a sample period and held there, graded by a failing mutant.
- [ ] **Bench:** with the DUT following a CRF talker, its own talker's presentation times measured against the followed stream's timing points within ±5 % of a sample period.

Relates to #629 and #74.

comments.body:
[A10] Assignment for [A659]: #632, which also closes #764. Branch `632-764-media-phase` from dev e26f1816.

Read #764's investigation report (the newest [A658] comment on #764) first: the measured numbers and the fix proposal are the brief.

**Ruling on the mechanism.** The phase term goes INSIDE `KL_mmcm_drp_servo`, which stays the single media-clock master. This is #632's "not a second master". The measurements show the physical audio clock itself is off (the DUT's own CRF output, not only the AAF timestamps), so the grid aligner alone cannot satisfy IEEE 1722-2016 10.8. #632's "feeds the grid aligner's lock target" becomes item 3 below.

1. **Phase detector.** For each accepted CRF PDU of the followed stream, compute the phase d between the DUT's presentation time for the matching sample and the CRF timestamp. Fold it into ±Ps/2 in fixed point, because Ps is not an integer number of ns. Average it over the servo's window.
2. **Phase term in the servo.** Make the loop type 2 against that phase, with the existing rate loop kept as damping.
   - The phase bandwidth is well below the rate loop's.
   - The phase shift is slew-limited, so the audio clock stays glitch-free (no slip, TDM frame continuity).
   - Carry the integrator's dropped LSBs: `ew_r >>> KI_SHIFT_P` floors odd errors, which gives a drift of up to 1.95 ns/s in #764.
3. **Deterministic packet grid.** Remove the fixed −0.46 Ps between the AAF packet grid and the DUT's own CRF output: set the aligner's lock target, or fold the constant into the detector. Also phase `KL_crf_tx`'s event divider, so that both outputs of the one clock domain fall on whole periods (IEEE 1722-2016 4.3.5).
4. **Re-acquisition.** After HOLDOVER→ACQUIRE, after an `mr` toggle and after a reference timestamp step, the phase is re-acquired with a bound. The restart signalling of #761 stays consistent.
5. **Contract and proof.**
   - Write the per-source phase contract (CRF; AAF as the follow-on) in `docs/design/MEDIA_CLOCK_FOLLOWING.md`.
   - Simulation cases, each pulled into ±5 % of Ps and held, each with a failing planted mutant per loop term:
     - an arbitrary engagement phase;
     - a reference phase step;
     - a local-oscillator ramp of several ppm;
     - a 15 s holdover;
     - re-engagement through INTERNAL.
   - Run the full suite sweep, route-1x1 within the resource gate and the timing floor, and the docs gates.
   - The bench proof (the #764 method) follows from the manager after merge. This lane has no bench access.

**STOP conditions:**
- any register-map layout change beyond new read-only status fields;
- any top-level port change;
- any change outside the media-clock chain, its tests and its docs.

Clauses: Milan v1.2 7.6.1; IEEE 1722-2016 10.6-10.8 (Eq. 15 and 16), 4.3.5.

[A659] TAKEN
Branch: 632-764-media-phase (from dev e26f1816)
Authoritative references: Milan v1.2 7.6.1; IEEE 1722-2016 10.6, 10.7, 10.8 (Equations 15 and 16), 4.3.5; assignment https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/632#issuecomment-6284510903; #764 report https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/764#issuecomment-6283948176
Interpreted scope: per the mechanism ruling, a phase term inside KL_mmcm_drp_servo, which stays the single media-clock master. A per-PDU phase detector compares the followed CRF stream's timestamps with the DUT's own presentation time of the matching packet-grid sample, folded into +/-Ps/2 exactly (Ps = 62500/3 ns) and averaged over the servo window. The loop becomes type 2 against that phase, with the rate loop kept as damping, a bandwidth well below it, a slew limit on the phase correction, and the integrator's dropped LSBs carried. The fixed packet-grid to CRF-output offset is removed and KL_crf_tx's event divider is phased from the aligned packet grid, so both outputs of the one clock domain fall on whole periods. Phase re-acquisition is bounded after HOLDOVER to ACQUIRE, an mr toggle and a reference timestamp step, with the restart signalling unchanged. The per-source phase contract (CRF, with AAF as the follow-on) goes into docs/design/MEDIA_CLOCK_FOLLOWING.md. No register-map change beyond new read-only status fields, no top-level port change, nothing outside the media-clock chain, its tests and its docs.
Validation plan: new self-checking simulation cases (arbitrary engagement phase, reference phase step, local-oscillator ramp of several ppm, 15 s holdover, re-engagement through INTERNAL), each pulled into +/-5 % of Ps and held, each with a planted mutant per loop term; lint_rtl --check; the full Verilator suite sweep; syn/yosys/run.sh; route-1x1 with the resource gate and the timing floor; the docs gates.
Blockers: none

[A10] Addendum to the #632 assignment (issuecomment-6284510903): the phase reference point, and the in/out latencies.

IEEE 1722-2016 ties a timestamp to the instant a sample crosses the media interface. Today neither path compensates the fixed latencies between the 1722 buffers and the interface (`docs/design/TIME_SYNC.md`):
- **Listener.** Render latency equals the presentation time offset at the crossbar's input grid. The post-grid delays to the TDM pin are measured but not compensated: the crossbar, the bank walk (9 axis cycles) and the per-slot adopt wait.
- **Talker.** The capture timestamp is the media tick's sample time plus the presentation offset. The captured frame's age at the tick (256 to 785 axis cycles under CRF, fixed per lock) and the per-pair offset ((3 − p) pair periods) are not subtracted.

Added items:
1. **Phase reference = the interface instant.** The phase detector compares the followed CRF timing points with the DUT's media events AT THE TDM PINS: the frame sync and slot timing, not the internal grid.
2. **Fold the fixed in/out terms in as measured constants, per shape and per slot.**
   - Talker: the AAF and CRF timestamps account for the capture age and the pair offset.
   - Listener: the post-grid pin delay is counted against the presentation time offset.
   - Derive each constant from the shape parameters; never mirror a number. Document each in MEDIA_CLOCK_FOLLOWING.md and TIME_SYNC.md.
3. **Prove it at the pins.** Using the existing pin decoder (the one that timestamps each slot's MSB edge), add a simulation check that grades a TDM slot's pin instant against its AAF timestamp and against the DUT's CRF output timestamp, within ±5 % of Ps. Add a planted control that drops one latency term and fails.
4. **Account for the measured constant.** Report how much of the constant −0.46 Ps between the packet grid and the DUT's CRF output in #764 these terms explain, before choosing the aligner target in item 3 of the assignment.

[A10] Second addendum to #632 (it replaces item 1 of issuecomment-6284578201). Design requirement: several media interfaces (several TDM or I2S ports) share ONE media clock as their reference.

1. **One phase reference per media clock domain, not per interface.** The servo is the single master of the domain. The phase detector compares the followed CRF timing points against the domain's own media event: one defined point in the media-clock chain that every interface derives from. It never compares against a particular interface's pins. This is Milan v1.2's CLOCK_DOMAIN model: one domain, one clock source, any number of streams and interfaces.
2. **Per-interface in and out latency constants, relative to that domain event.**
   - Each interface has its own capture age, pair or slot offset, and post-grid pin delay, derived from that interface's own parameters.
   - They are applied to the AAF and CRF timestamps and to the presentation of the streams that interface carries.
   - Result: every interface's pin instants fall on the same CRF timing points (IEEE 1722-2016 4.3.5; 10.8 within ±5 % of Ps).
   - Adding an interface adds its constants, never a second loop.
3. **Prove it with two interfaces.** Use a simulation shape with at least two interfaces whose latencies differ. A synthetic shape is fine if no in-tree shape has two. Grade each interface's pin instant (the slot-MSB pin decoder) against the same CRF timing points. Add a planted control that drops or swaps one interface's constant and fails. The shipping 1x1 TDM8 shape stays graded as before.
4. **Document it.** Record the domain-reference and per-interface-constant contract in `docs/design/MEDIA_CLOCK_FOLLOWING.md` and `docs/design/TIME_SYNC.md`.

Items 2 to 4 of issuecomment-6284578201 stand as written, now per interface.

[A659] REVIEW READY
Branch: `632-764-media-phase` (from dev `e26f1816`; not pushed from this lane)
Commit: f1fda3f1f87c64801e436e129326b5bd5952bf20

Changed:
- `KL_mmcm_drp_servo`: a phase term inside the one media-clock master. Per accepted CRF PDU, the domain media event less the CRF timestamp, folded exactly into +/-Ps/2 in 1/3 ns (Ps = 62,500/3 ns). The window phase is the sample sum over the nominal 256 PDUs, capped at 264 samples. It enters the integrator one window late, clamped, so the loop is type 2 against phase with the rate loop as damping (phase pole 0.944 per window, 8.9 s; rate pole 0.70), and the pull is slew-limited to 0.5 ppm. The integrator keeps 8 fractional bits (the #764 floor leak). Outside LOCKED, at an `mr` toggle, a broken reference history, or a PHC step or slew, the term lets go. `MCSRV_STAT[9]` (reserved, read-only) reads settled inside +/-5 % of Ps.
- `KL_media_domain_event` (new): one phase reference per clock domain, the frame-timing owner's closing-pair strobe back-dated by its derived marker latency. `KL_media_if_latency_pkg` (new) derives each interface's constants from its own parameters.
- `KL_crf_tx` stamps every 96th domain event (its /512 divider and crossing are retired). The AAF talkers stamp the instant the capture crossbar banks with each frame (`KL_chan_map_capture`), so capture age and pair offset leave the timestamp. `KL_crf_rx` publishes its consumed timing point.
- Two `milan_dp` fixtures re-timed for the CRF talker's domain-event cadence, their checks unchanged: the #726 counters TX wrap leg runs `400000 x slots / 8` cycles, and the nxn legs wait 200,000 clocks for a CRF PDU (the media-tick fallback on nxn4c, whose TDM master that fixture leaves unclocked).
- Docs: `docs/design/MEDIA_CLOCK_FOLLOWING.md` Phase alignment (per-source contract, constants per interface, the -0.46 Ps accounting, the proof table), `docs/design/TIME_SYNC.md`, `docs/testing/TESTING.md`, CHANGELOG.
No top-level port and no register-map layout change.

Validation (at the commit above unless noted):
- `make -C tb/verilator/media_phase`: three interfaces of one domain graded at every slot's MSB pin, and ten cases (engagement from +0.44 and -0.36 Ps, a 0.37 Ps reference step, a 4 ppm ramp, a 15 s holdover, 15 s at INTERNAL, an `mr` toggle, a 27 us PHC slew, a talker 4 % faster than it declares, the integrator carry), each pulled into +/-5 % of Ps within its bound and held: pass.
- `make -C tb/verilator/media_phase mutants MUTANT_JOBS=4` at `e85df091` (no media_phase or RTL file changed since): 27 checks, 0 failures; 17 of 17 planted defects fail their named checks.
- Full sweep, `scripts/run_all_suites.sh`, shards 0-3: 64 of 64 suites pass. Shard 0: 15/15, 52,903 checks, `milan_dp` included; `tsn_fuzz` with tsn-gen at the workflow's pin (164 + 677 field checks). Shard 1, at `e85df091`: 16/16, 331,441 checks; the later commits change three `milan_dp` fixture files that no shard-1 suite compiles. Shard 2: 16/17 under the runner, 262,022 checks; `capture_coherence` (the `[PIN]` leg and its 25-mutant campaign) hit the 2,400 s wall clock on the two CPUs that keep its campaign at two builds, and was re-run alone inside the same budget: pass, campaign 35 of 35. Shard 3: 16/16, 1,540,268 checks.
- `python3 scripts/lint_rtl.py --check`: PASS, 89 <= ratchet 89. `syn/yosys/run.sh`: 59 of 59 tops pass. The 49 docs-workflow gates: all pass.
- route-1x1 under `docs/testing/PP_SHADOW_BASELINE_RECIPE.md` at `a6ae20f9` (RTL identical to the commit above), `pp_resource_gate.py check`: exit 0. LUT 49,644 (+31 of +500), FF 52,641 (+288 of +600), slice 15,785 (+60 of +80), RAMB36/RAMB18/DSP +0, WNS +0.276 ns, WHS +0.032 ns, route complete.

Acceptance criteria:
- Simulation: a reference phase step pulled into +/-5 % of Ps and held, graded by failing mutants: met (`media_phase` `step`; the assignment's five cases and the addenda's pin and two-interface proofs likewise).
- Bench: not met in this lane (no bench access); the #764 method follows after merge. So the PR body says "Relates to #632" and "Relates to #764".

Open risks/questions:
1. Decision needed, the listener: its post-grid pin delay cannot be counted against the presentation time offset, because the render path presents by fill (8 events after accept, #386), not at the timestamp. Its constants are derived and documented; a timestamp-driven render is a listener-datapath change outside the media-clock chain.
2. Decision for the merge: the area budget asks an image-moving merge to re-record its resource endpoints on the merge result. That record and its budget text lie outside the media-clock chain, so this lane did not write them.
3. AAF following keeps the rate loop alone; a phase reference for it needs a decision on presentation offsets that are not whole periods.
4. Four builder and configuration comments still name the retired `KL_crf_tx` /512 divider; outside the chain, proposed as a follow-up.

[A659] STOP
Head: 2ff30f0dc5e89be46f8103272883885e8553f4b8 (branch 632-764-media-phase, twelve new commits on f1fda3f1; not pushed; dev 78ca9bdf not merged)

Stopped on one item: R678-1-F1 (the listener presenting each sample at the pin at its presentation time) needs a decision before it can be built inside the gates the same round 2 ruling sets. Every other round 2 item is done at the head.

Why F1 is a decision, measured before any design was chosen:
- Storage. Presenting at the timestamp holds each sample for the offset less its arrival lead, about 1.9 ms at the 2 ms default, about 96 events: 128 event rows per 8-channel stream where KL_render_setpoint keeps 32. Out-of-context synthesis at the AX7101 1x1 parameters: 456 LUT (128 LUTRAM) at 32 rows, 1,006 LUT (512 LUTRAM) at 128, +550 LUT for the storage alone. route-1x1 headroom is 404 LUT and 8 slices at this head; RAMB tolerance is 0, and a block-RAM queue needs two or three RAMB18 (the parity-split rows take a write port each). The depacketizer frame FIFO is 2,048 bytes, about 8 shipping PDUs, under the 14 a 2 ms hold needs.
- Contract. Any form replaces the #386 render law (fill 8 events after accept, its rails, the #387 and #645 recentres) graded by render_setpoint, milan_dp, follow_ring, milan_dp_gm_steps and milan_dp_render.
- Interfaces. One pop per stream cannot land two interfaces whose post-grid delays differ by a frame on one presentation time without a per-interface frame delay; the Arty DAC path (KL_i2s_playback) keeps its own fill law and elastic FIFO.
Options: (a) a timestamp-snapped render queue, LUTRAM (about 550 LUT of storage plus logic) or block RAM (two or three RAMB18); (b) a presentation gate at a deepened depacketizer FIFO (one RAMB36), which also delays the loopback ring and the DAC tap. Either needs an accepted route-1x1 re-record, a supported offset range (the queue depth), a rule for late and too-early PDUs, and whether the retired Arty DAC path is in scope.

Done at the head:
- R678-1-F3: each phase sample unwrapped against a tracking reference before summing, the window phase re-folded; settled needs the window phase and every sample of four full windows in band. On f1fda3f1 the new detector cases read balanced, 129:127, 160:96 and jittered half-period samples as theta 0, 244, 7,812 and 10,678 (of about 31,250) and settled on in-band means of out-of-band samples; all now read the half-period phase, pull at the slew limit and never settle. Closed loop at +Ps/2 and -Ps/2 with 8 ns truncation and +/-48 ns jitter: in band after 26.4 and 26.6 s, never settled outside the band.
- R678-1-F4: the snapshot reads the hold on its own edge; mr, the term disabled, a broken history, not-LOCKED, a PHC step and the slew level each placed one cycle before, on and after the closing edge commit 0, 0 and the whole correction.
- R678-1-F2: every output's offset applied rounded up to whole periods by KL_crf_tx's Equation (14) rule in one multiplier-free rounder (KL_mtt_round) that the AAF talkers and the CRF output both stamp (KL_crf_tx ROUND_MTT_P = 0); GET_STREAM_INFO reads the applied value (2,010,000 set, 2,020,834 read; the raw value sat 0.48 Ps off). Four AAF outputs and the CRF output with 0, 1, 20,833, 20,834, 62,500, 2,000,000, 2,010,000, 4,294,958,333 and 0xFFFFFFFF ns, at reset and at run time: worst AAF-to-CRF phase 1.0 ns. Equation (14) is not idempotent in whole ns for period counts that are no multiple of three; that is documented.
- R677-1-F1: the blend closes each frame on its I2S pair, back-dated by the I2S front end's latency. Graded with sample values at both interfaces' pins through the capture crossbar's bank, six reset phases: I2S pair -29 to -11 ns, every TDM pair +11 to +29 ns from the banked instant. That grade found a second defect: KL_aaf_capture_i2s (and the flat aaf_talker_i2s it was split from) presented each pair on the next strobe, one frame late; both fixed.
- R677-1-F2, F3: phcstep case and the step-hold mutant; settled timing, mirror and fold-range cases with their mutants. R677-1-F4: media_phase timed at 578 s for its whole default target. R677-1-F5 and R678-1-R1 applied as written.
- Mutants: the media_phase campaign plants 28 defects (11 new: the tracking fold, the window re-fold, settled on the mean, the snapshot hold, settled as the engaged bit, the fold-range guard, the PHC step hold, the offset rounding, the CRF output's raw row, the blend's old closing pair, the late I2S pop); all 28 fail their named checks after 18 clean controls pass.

Gates at the head (or an ancestor the later commits leave untouched for that gate): full sweep, 64 of 64 suites, 2,187,770 checks, 0 failures; media_phase mutants 46 checks, 0 failures; lint 89 <= ratchet 89; the 49 docs gates; the open-synthesis gate, 60 of 60 tops, and the six changed tops again; the builder bank (all pass, one not run for its recorded reason); route-1x1 within the resource gate.

Resources, route-1x1 against the record: LUT 49,709 (+96 of +500), FF 52,760 (+407 of +600), slices 15,797 (+72 of +80), RAMB36/RAMB18 74/25 (+0), DSP 13 (-1: the CRF output's own converter is no longer elaborated), WNS +0.305 ns, WHS +0.036 ns, route complete, gate exit 0.

Evidence: the round 2 receipts in the hand-off packet (receipts/round2/, index regenerated).

[A10] Owner decision 2026-10-21 on the listener presentation at the pin, R678-1-F1. It was scoped out of PR #770 by https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/770#issuecomment-6306187740.

- **Built now.** The owner chose "the option that scales up and down the best and the easier to port and multiplatform". The release milestone moves one week, to 11-07, so this lands before the release qualification.
- **Option (a), a timestamp-snapped render queue after the depacketizer.**
  - A vendor-neutral inferred memory with no device primitives. Its depth is derived from the supported maximum offset and the shape, never mirrored. Synthesis maps it to LUTRAM or block RAM by size.
  - It is per stream, so it scales across NxN streams, several interfaces and small parts. Each interface's read applies its own derived post-grid delay against the one domain media event, per the owner requirement of 2026-10-20 on this issue.
  - Option (b), the depacketizer-FIFO gate, is not taken. It is a fixed block at PDU granularity, it also delays the loopback ring and the DAC tap, and it has no per-interface answer.
- **Budget, an owner exception.** About 2-3 RAMB18, or the LUTRAM equivalent, at the 1x1 shape, with an accepted route-1x1 re-record. Every other resource bar is unchanged.
- **Delivery.** PR #770 round 4, after round 3. The full assignment follows on #770, with:
  - the replaced #386 render law and its five suites re-graded;
  - the supported offset range;
  - the late and too-early PDU rule (IEEE 1722-2016 presentation time, Milan v1.2);
  - the pin-level proof on two interfaces with different delays.

[A10] Owner refinement, 2026-10-21, to https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/issues/632#issuecomment-6309219099: the render queue is **block RAM** at every shape.

- **Form.** An inferred, synchronous-read memory with a block-RAM style hint and no device primitives, so it stays portable.
- **Budget.** One 32 Kbit row set per 8-channel stream at 48 kHz with the 2 ms default offset: about 1 RAMB36 or 2 RAMB18 per stream, and about 8 RAMB36 at 8x8. It scales with the media rate and the supported maximum offset, and the depth is derived from them.
- **Rejected.** The LUTRAM mapping is not taken.
- **Required in round 4.** Out-of-context synthesis at 1x1 and at 8x8, reporting the block RAM, LUT and FF figures, plus the accepted route-1x1 re-record.

[A659] STOP

milan-fpga head: 32fb8fc26acf7dedc507512d7a455898a26afd84 (branch 632-764-media-phase, PR #770; not pushed; ten commits on 2ff30f0d, no rebase, no amend)
Processor head: none. Branch 632-sinfo-notify-stored stays at processor main 08023123: no processor commit until the ruling below.
STOP condition hit (round 3 assignment, https://github.com/kebag-logic/milan-fpga/pull/770#issuecomment-6306591168): "the processor fix needs more than the one gather change".

**What fails.** The fix as ruled replaces E_SINFO's `GATHER_EXT rd=6, GSI(3)` with `READ_ST rd=6, RGN_DYN + SEL_PTOFF`. The processor's dynamic store reads a row no controller has written as 0, with its valid bit clear (`KL_aecp_dyn_state`: `ptoff_r` resets to 0, `ptoff_v_r` to 0). Meanwhile the integrator serves the factory 2 ms. Two consequences:
- A SET of the factory value on a never-set row compares 2,000,000 with 0 and pushes.
- A SET of 0 compares 0 with 0 and pushes nothing, although the offset in force moves from 2 ms to 0. The pin and the base both push here.

The `[NOTIFY]` notify leg sets no row before the section, so R677-2's step 1 runs on a never-set row.

**Measured.** The committed `milan_dp` `[NOTIFY]` SET_STREAM_INFO case, 1x1 notify leg, real datapath and processor. Each microcode was applied uncommitted to the submodule at its pin `2cbed0a9`, which was then restored clean:

| Processor | step 1 (2,000,000, held) | step 2 (2,010,000) | step 3 (2,010,000 again) | step 4 (2,020,834) | SET 0 on a never-set row (disposable probe) | leg |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| current pin (gate reads GET_STREAM_INFO word 3) | 0 | 1 | **1** | **0** | 1 | 444 checks, 3 failures |
| (a) as ruled: one read of the stored row | **1** | 1 | 0 | 1 | **0** | 444 checks, 2 failures |
| (b) the stored row once a controller set it (`RGN_DYNV` read), GET_STREAM_INFO word 3 before | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | 444 checks, 0 failures |
| expected (R677-2's column; the probe by 5.4.5.2) | 0 | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | |

Option (b) is the store's own idiom, as E_SCFG uses it for #178: a valid read, a COMPARE and a BR_STATUS. It adds five microcode words and keeps the gather on the never-set arm. With (b) at 32fb8fc2:
- the notify leg passes, 441 checks, 0 failures;
- the planted control (the gate comparing with the applied readback again) is caught at "[NOTIFY] SET_STREAM_INFO step 3".

At the current pin the case fails steps 3 and 4, as recorded. (b) leaves one residue: before its first SET, a factory row that is not a whole number of periods compares with its applied value. No shipping config has one; every factory row is 2 ms.

**Decision needed:**
- (a) as ruled, with R677-2's step 1 re-specified and the never-set SET 0 recorded as a follow-up; or
- (b) as above.

The processor PR, its test (an identical SET pushes nothing, a changed SET pushes once) and its planted defect then follow the ruling.

**Done at 32fb8fc2:**
- R678-2-F1: every rounded offset keeps bit 32. The CRF output adds it into its 64-bit timestamp. GET_STREAM_INFO reads a row past 32 bits as 0xFFFFFFFF. The grader works at full width (33-bit rows, 64-bit CRF timestamps against Equation 14 and the grid) at 4,294,958,333 / 4,294,958,334 / 0xFFFFFFFF, in reset and at run time. Four carry mutants, the truncation among them, are each killed at a named check. The wrap claim is corrected in the banner, the design doc and the PR body.
- R677-2-F2: `det afterhold` and `hold_keeps_ref`.
- R677-2-F3, and the residues R677-2-R1..R5 and R678-2-R1..R2.
- The "what a controller reads" claim is scoped to GET_STREAM_INFO. The SET echo against the applied readback is documented (5.4.2.9, 5.4.2.10.2).
- The applied-value-changes-without-a-SET case is recorded as a follow-up.

**Found on the way, fixed:**
- The carry's first form, one indexed concatenation target, synthesized to 0 cells in Yosys. The open-synthesis gate still printed PASS. Now two indexed writes, 1,215 cells. A gate that accepts a zero-cell top is a follow-up.
- The case's step 1 premise ("the offset held") holds only on the timed notify leg. The other legs set output 0 to 750,000 ns first, so the case now runs on the timed leg alone.

**Gates at 32fb8fc2** (or at the ancestor named, where nothing later touches that gate's inputs):
- `milan_dp`, run leg by leg: every leg except notify gives 14 tallies, 11,629 checks, 0 failures. At this pin `sim_pool.py` starts no leg after the designed notify failure, so each leg runs on its own.
